prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the continuous 3D geometry of a living room roughly 4 to 5 metres deep, bounded by a couch and coffee table on the lower left (1 to 2 metres away), a TV stand on the lower right (1 to 1.5 metres away), a round dog bed and rocking chair along the right wall (2.5 to 4 metres away), and a back wall with a sliding glass door. No people are in the scene, while a dog in the center-front starts about 4 metres away near the back door in frame 1 and walks directly toward the camera wearer, reaching roughly 3.5 metres in frame 2, 2.5 metres in frame 3, 1.5 metres in frame 4, and under 1 metre (entering lower reach and partly cropped at the bottom edge) in frame 5 as the camera pitches downward. Across the frames, the foreground coffee table (0.5 to 1 metre to the dog's left in frames 4 and 5) and the TV stand (about 1 metre to the dog's right) remain within or just beyond arm's reach of the camera wearer, partially cropped at the bottom and side edges. Compared to the RGB image, the depth map clearly separates the approaching dog's silhouette and the raised rims of the dog bed and coffee table tray from the similarly toned carpet and backlit floor. However, the depth map is unreliable around the bright sliding glass door and thin wire dog crate in the background, which merge into a flat black far-plane void, and it loses fine internal contours on the dark TV screen and cluttered table items.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates discrete foreground and background objects on a black canvas, detecting the dog in the center of frames 2, 3, and 4 as it walks from roughly 3.5 metres to 1.5 metres in front of the camera wearer while facing and looking upward toward the viewpoint in frame 4. It also segments the rocking chair near the back right wall (about 3.5 to 4 metres away, 1 to 2 metres behind and to the right of the dog) across all five frames, along with potted plants on the upper left window sill and above the chair in frames 1 through 3. Unlike the RGB image, where the white-and-brown dog in frame 1 blends into the overexposed glare of the back glass door and where the plants overlap the chair frame, the segmentation masks provide sharp object boundaries for the detected instances in frames 2 through 4. However, the map is highly incomplete and unreliable for full scene layout: it completely misses the dog in frame 1 (at 4 metres, misclassifying its hindquarters as a chair) and frame 5 (at 1 metre, partly out of view at the bottom), and omits major nearby structures within 1 to 2 metres such as the coffee table, TV stand, dog crate, and round dog bed. Additionally, it mislabels the pile of blankets on the couch arm on the lower left (1.5 to 2 metres away, within or near arm's reach) as a backpack in frames 1 and 2 and as a potted plant in frame 3.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost entirely empty across the five frames because no other people or human hands—including the camera wearer's own arms—are visible within the field of view. Because the pose detector only targets human keypoints, the approaching dog (moving from 4 metres to 1 metre in front of the camera wearer) and all surrounding furniture, walls, and floor surfaces are completely absent from the map. In frame 3, the map displays a single small yellow body skeleton in the lower-left foreground (roughly 1.5 to 2 metres to the left of the camera wearer and about 1 metre to the left of the approaching dog). Checking the RGB strip shows that this skeleton is a false positive triggered by the folded blankets and clothing draped over the arm of the couch, falsely implying a person facing right. Consequently, the pose map offers no usable spatial information for this scene and is unreliable where cluttered fabrics mimic human limb geometry.
